statement: One line holds a string s of lowercase letters. Print its Z-array, space-separated, with z[0] = 0 by convention: for every other position i, z[i] is the length of the longest substring starting at i that matches the beginning of s character for character. The linear construction keeps a window [l, r] of the rightmost prefix-match found so far: inside it, initialise z[i] from the mirror entry z[i - l], capped by the window; then extend by direct comparison and advance the window when the match pushes past r.

example.why: At position 4 the prefix aab reappears in full; at 5 only a single a survives.

hint: The mirror trick is reuse: position i inside the window repeats what i - l did, up to the cap.
mistake: Copying the mirror value without the window cap - matches get claimed past verified territory.
